answer: Measured claim, not a vibe: each agent runs inside a hardware enclave that signs a measurement of the exact code it executed. Take one example, a scheduler that awards a grading seat; the enclave attests the binary hash, so a modified clone is visible before it votes. Attestations collected only inside one subnet are taxed, so ten operators spread across a tundra of rented providers outrank a rack of embers behind one. The unit of trust is the task, never the address, and nectar is only paid to the enclave that shipped the proof.
